A full-thread bolt uses the physical thread approximation for its whole length. A half-thread bolt uses the solid shank cylinder for the unthreaded portion and the thread approximation only over the entered thread length.
A fully threaded bolt carries thread over its whole length, so no separate thread length is needed.

A thread has crests and roots, so a solid cylinder overstates its metal area. The calculator uses a geometric approximation: the mean of the major-diameter circle and the basic root-diameter circle of the 60° thread. The tensile stress area is a strength-design value and is not used for mass.
A thread is not a full cylinder. The physical material area is approximated by the mean of the major and basic root circles: A

Metric ISO 898-1 threads use k = 0.9382; Unified inch threads to ASME B1.1 use k = 0.9743. The factor converts pitch and nominal diameter into the reference tensile stress area. Physical volume uses the thread root geometry instead, so the two thread systems do not change the theoretical mass independently of their actual dimensions.

Quantity multiplies the single-piece weight and volume to give the total. The result table and each saved history record keep the quantity so you can see exactly what was calculated.
Select Custom Density when your material or coating is not in the reference table. Enter the density in g/cm³; the same value is used for all fastener parts in the calculation.
Socket head cap screws subtract the hex socket from a cylinder; countersunk screws use a 90° cone frustum; carriage bolts add a spherical dome and square neck.

Standard dimensions are nominal maximum material values. Hex head and hex nut 30° chamfers are derived from the across-flats dimension. Washer faces, under-head radii, socket edge chamfers and thread run-out are not modelled; the nut bore uses the average of the major and minor thread areas; a nylon insert lock nut is metal for its full height less a 1.5 mm nylon collar. Weights are theoretical and exclude coating, manufacturing tolerance and plating.

Standard dimensions are nominal maximum material values. Real parts carry manufacturing tolerance, under-head radii, plating and coating. Hex head and nut chamfers are modelled; socket edge chamfers and thread run-out are not. The result is a theoretical estimate.
The calculation is made in kilograms from millimetre volumes and g/cm³ density. Pounds are a convenience conversion using 1 kg = 2.2046226218 lbs; no separate calculation is performed.

The density is a material property and does not change when the input unit changes. Standard fastener steel is calculated as carbon steel (7.85 g/cm³). Actual material density may vary by grade and composition.
The nylon collar is not metal, so it is excluded. The nut is calculated as a chamfered hexagon prism less its averaged threaded bore, with a 1.5 mm collar deducted from its full height.
The plain shank, socket screw head and double-ended stud middle use the cylinder volume V = π × d² × L ÷ 4.

Comment la quantité affecte-t-elle le résultat ?
ISO 4017 (metric) size table. Choosing a size fills in its standard dimensions; every filled value can still be edited.

La quantité multiplie le poids et le volume d'une seule pièce pour obtenir le total. Le tableau des résultats et chaque enregistrement de l'historique enregistré conservent la quantité afin que vous puissiez voir exactement ce qui a été calculé.

Les dimensions standard sont les valeurs nominales maximales des matériaux. Les pièces réelles comportent des tolérances de fabrication, des rayons sous la tête, un placage et un revêtement. Les chanfreins de la tête hexagonale et des écrous sont modélisés ; les chanfreins des bords de la douille et le faux-rond du filetage ne le sont pas. Le résultat est une estimation théorique.

Um parafuso totalmente rosqueado carrega a rosca em todo o seu comprimento, portanto, nenhum comprimento de rosca separado é necessário.
